moat_against: Merchandise distribution is contestable: Patterson/Benco regionally, Amazon and direct manufacturer sales, thin ~5% operating margin
ROIC faded from 15.5% (FY2021) to ~8.0% (FY2023-25) — at, not above, the cost of capital through the recent cycle
Leverage: net debt $2.951B is 5.3x normalized OE; buybacks and acquisitions were debt-funded as OCF weakened in FY2023
Customer base is small practices with no contractual lock-in on supplies; Oct 2023 cyber incident showed operational fragility
moat_for: #1 scale in dental distribution — world's largest provider to office-based dental/medical practitioners, dense logistics network
Henry Schein One / Dentrix practice-management software installed base creates switching friction beyond merchandise
Mix shift to specialty products (implants), own brand and technology lifting gross margin 27.8% (FY2020) to 31.1% (FY2025), 31.8% in Q2 2026
KKR anchor stake (12%, May 2025, right to 19.9%) and two board seats driving a >$200M operating-income value-creation program
moat_justification: World's largest distributor to office-based dental and medical practitioners: scale, dense logistics and the Henry Schein One / Dentrix software installed base give moderate switching friction, and mix shift to specialty products and own brand has lifted gross margin from 27.8% (FY2020) to 31.1% (FY2025). But merchandise distribution itself has low switching costs, manufacturers can sell direct, and measured returns have faded: roic_proxy fell from 15.5% (FY2021) to 8.0-8.2% (FY2023-25), roughly at the cost of capital, with operating margin stuck near 5%. A moderate/narrow moat, not a wide one.
name: Henry Schein, Inc.
one_liner: Durable #1 dental/medical distributor, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $84.58 (weighted IRR 10.2%, IV@15 $50.56); it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$51, and the bear case (7.8%) sizes the verdict.
